A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same diffusion-RL study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison, including the additional appendix experiments in v2.pdf.

before.justification: v1.pdf reports original SD3.5-Medium fine-tuning experiments, comparisons of objectives and likelihood estimators, ablations, and quantitative and qualitative results in Section 4 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v2.pdf retains those experiments and adds original unseen-category evaluations, FLUX.1-Dev fine-tuning results, and repeated-run measurements in Appendix E, Tables 6–8.

M1.justification: The displayed PAR objective changes its squared regression term from positive to negative in Section 3.3 and Appendix B, Eq. (10). This is a limited objective correction; Algorithm 1 and the other method components remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish a corresponding implementation change.

E1.justification: Table 6 adds evaluation on unseen GenEval object classes and counting scenarios, extending the tested input distribution. Existing GenEval, OCR, Pick-a-Pic training, and DrawBench evaluation coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the original experiments is unchanged, including FlowGRPO, AWM, DiffusionNFT, and pretrained generator baselines. The added evaluations reuse existing methods and baselines. Newly discussed AWR, DPPO, Q-score matching, and QUATRO are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Table 7 adds a fine-tuning experiment using FLUX.1-Dev with PEPG, ELBO estimation, and ODE sampling; v1 fine-tuned SD3.5-Medium and used FLUX only as a baseline. The original experimental settings and hyperparameter Tables 3–4 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds checks of generalization to unseen GenEval categories and applicability to another backbone in Tables 6–7. Existing objective, likelihood, sampler, and ELBO-weighting ablations are retained. The expanded clipping discussion does not introduce a new isolated clipping experiment.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates without run counts or uncertainty. Table 8 introduces three independent PEPG/PAR runs with means and standard deviations, plus runtime variability including trajectory EPG. This substantially changes statistical reporting for the central claims, although the caption invokes overlapping confidence intervals without specifying them.

E6.justification: Tables 6–8 add substantial result sets covering generalization, another fine-tuned backbone, and repeated-run quality and timing. Examples include unseen-category GenEval scores of 0.93 for the proposed method and 0.90 for Flow-GRPO, and 0.93 for fine-tuned FLUX. Original Tables 1–5 and figure results remain unchanged; the additions are not revisions of those scores.

T1.justification: v2 corrects the PAR regression sign, changes the trajectory-likelihood equality to an approximation, and adds an explicit KL-penalized proximal optimization problem for PEPG. Appendix B also expands the stop-gradient explanation. Theorem 3.1's target distribution and the remaining proof structure are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and principal conclusion retain the claim that likelihood estimation matters more than policy-gradient loss design. The headline GenEval and efficiency claims are unchanged. Added appendix evidence supports these existing contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly acknowledges limited architectural and benchmark coverage and the absence of output-diversity evaluation. Section 4.3 adds the interpretation that clipping may slightly hinder optimization, while Appendix E adds interpretations of spatial performance, generalization, and seed variability.

D1.justification: The computation details in Appendix C, implementation descriptions in Appendix D, Algorithm 1, and hyperparameter Tables 3–4 are unchanged. No new implementation or resource-access instructions accompany the added experiments; repeated-run disclosure is covered under E5.

R1.justification: v2 adds an EPG–AWR distinction in Section 3.1 and discussions of DPPO, Q-score matching, and QUATRO in Appendix A. These provide limited extensions of research positioning, including distinguishing PEPG's proximal objective from QUATRO's trust-region bound.

P1.justification: v2 revises the PEPG explanation, specifies KL-regularized REINFORCE terminology, expands discussion and proof commentary, and adds limitations and acknowledgments. The main narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 6–8 and reflows existing material, including placing Figures 4–5 together beneath Table 2 and relocating appendix displays. Existing figure images and Tables 1–5 retain their content and designs; there is no broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The added generalization, FLUX, and repeated-run evidence modestly strengthens the unchanged conclusions, while the PAR sign correction and explicit limitations improve precision. The gains are constrained by sparse documentation of the new tests and Table 8's reporting problems: it discusses confidence intervals while displaying standard deviations and lists trajectory EPG at 0.93 under a timing header requiring GenEval ≥0.95.
